prs.title: Prove semantic correctness of parallel reversible schedules
prs.body:
## Summary

This integration checkpoint combines the already-green foundations from #72 and #73 and closes their remaining semantic interface:

- lift wire-disjoint gate commutation to gate-vs-program and program-vs-program commutation;
- relate membership in a flattened scheduled program back to its source layers;
- prove the layer-wise merged `parallelLayers` schedule has exactly the same computational-basis semantics as complete-left followed by complete-right execution;
- expose `ScheduledReversibleProgram.eval_parallel` and `eval_parallel_eq_seq`;
- retain the existing proof-bearing resource facts: exact gate-count additivity and depth equal to `max`.

## Why this matters for Nie/Vandaele

Figure-3 recursion needs the two child computations to share time slices. This PR proves that the low-depth merged schedule is not merely a resource annotation: it is semantically equal to the established sequential composition of the same child programs.

## Verification

Dedicated workflow `Reversible parallel semantics` passes on Lean 4.29.1 at commit `6795d59ef9a03ca642a100e6e1b561aaa0f2c37e` (run `34144325486`).

## Stack

This branch intentionally preserves both #72 (gate-level disjoint commutation) and #73 (proof-bearing parallel schedules) as parents, then adds the whole-schedule semantic bridge.

## Harness boundary

This is still reusable infrastructure. It does not yet instantiate the full Nie Figure-3 recursion or claim the uniform Vandaele Lemma 1 `O(k)` / `O(log k)` resource family.

prs.title: Lift disjoint wire embeddings to scheduled child certificates
prs.body:
## Summary

- stabilize `ScheduledWireEmbedding` on Lean 4.29;
- characterize the exact wire support of renamed X/CX/CCX gates;
- prove schedule wire renaming preserves validity, flattened program semantics, exact gate count, and certified depth;
- define disjoint embedding images and lift them automatically to cross-disjoint mapped gates, layers, schedules, and scheduled programs.

## Why this matters for Nie/Vandaele

The logarithmic-depth Figure-3 recursion places two child computations on disjoint subregisters and then merges their time slices. The recursion should prove disjointness once at the wire-embedding level, not redo gate-overlap arithmetic at every recursive layer. This PR supplies that reusable certificate.

## Verification

Dedicated workflow `Reversible embedding disjointness` passes on Lean 4.29.1 at commit `cb6b6df82997592adf5b9d02ba18422e27dd5cac`.

## Harness boundary

This PR proves transport and non-overlap only. It does not itself merge schedules or claim the full Vandaele Lemma 1 recursive family.
